title: Show Serve offices who lives in their district
body:
Serve offices keep asking the Chief of Staff "who actually lives in my district?" and we have no screen that answers it. The Constituents page shows one number (the district total), but gp-api already computes the age, household income, education, homeowner and children-at-home breakdowns on `GET /v1/contacts/stats`; they just never reach the page.

This adds a Serve-only "Your district" page at `/dashboard/contacts/district`, linked from a "See who lives in your district" link under the district stat card. It renders the totals and each breakdown as a share of the district, with the count beside it.

The page follows the Import history page's shape: `page.tsx` only checks Serve access, and the client component reads the stats with React Query. It uses `districtStatsQueryOptions`, the same query and cache key as the district stat card, so arriving from the Constituents page paints from cache, and a cold load shows the frame and skeletons right away. An office whose district is unresolvable is caught by `useDistrictResolution` first: the query stays disabled and the page says there is no data for the office. If the stats can't be read it shows a short unavailable message.

Also adds the route to `SERVE_ROUTE_PREFIXES` so a deep link selects the elected-office org after login (and to `SERVE_ONLY_DIRS` for the vocabulary check), a line in the assistants' product map, and a note in the contacts AGENTS.md. It also adds two events, `Contacts - District Profile Link Clicked` and `Contacts - District Profile Viewed`, with unit and E2E assertions and their provenance rows.
